title: Augmented simplicial polynomial scalar-extension model
statement: Let $A\to B$ and $A\to A'$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings. Let $\epsilon:P_\bullet\to B$ be an augmented simplicial $A$-algebra [def-trf-cotangent-resolution-data], with each $\epsilon_n$ surjective and with chosen $A$-algebra identifications $P_n\cong A[X_i:i\in I_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], where $I_n$ is any set. No quasi-isomorphism hypothesis on $\epsilon$ is imposed. Write $C=s(P_\bullet)$ for the alternating-face cochain complex, $C^{-n}=P_n$, with zero positive terms and differential $\sum_i(-1)^id_i$, and let $q:C\to B[0]$ be its augmentation. Then each $C^{-n}$ is free over $A$ on its monomials, and is flat: tensoring it with modules preserves exact sequences. More precisely, for every $A$-module $M$, coefficient expansion gives a natural module isomorphism $P_n\otimes_A M\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\mathbf N^{(I_n)}}M$, sending $(\sum_\alpha a_\alpha X^\alpha)\otimes m$ to $(a_\alpha m)_\alpha$, with inverse $(m_\alpha)_\alpha\mapsto\sum_\alpha X^\alpha\otimes m_\alpha$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Put $B'=B\otimes_A A'$ and $P'_n=P_n\otimes_A A'$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Tensoring the faces, degeneracies and augmentations defines an augmented simplicial $A'$-algebra $\epsilon':P'_\bullet\to B'$. Every $\epsilon'_n$ is surjective, and $P'_n\cong A'[X_i:i\in I_n]$ as an $A'$-algebra by the map $X^\alpha\otimes a'\mapsto a'X^\alpha$. Let $q':s(P'_\bullet)\to B'[0]$ be the resulting augmentation, let $T$ be termwise scalar extension, and let $Q_{A'}$ denote localization to $D(A')$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The identity maps on $P_n\otimes_A A'$ represent an isomorphism $\phi:Q_{A'}(TC)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_{A'}s(P'_\bullet)$ satisfying $Q_{A'}(q')\circ\phi=Q_{A'}(Tq)$, with $T(B[0])=B'[0]$.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof: the monomial-free terms of s(P) and the equality s(P) tensor A-prime = s(P tensor A-prime), with the prescribed augmentation; Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), polynomial and surjectivity conditions.

proof.text: Fix $n$ and put $E=\mathbf N^{(I_n)}$. Under the chosen polynomial identification, every element of $P_n$ has exactly one finite coefficient expansion $\sum_{\alpha\in E}a_\alpha X^\alpha$. Thus the family $(X^\alpha)_{\alpha\in E}$ is a basis by the definition of basis, and $C^{-n}=P_n$ is free. This uses no finiteness of $I_n$.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof: P_n is a free A-module; expand using the polynomial definition.

proof.text: For an $A$-module $M$, the rule $(p,m)\mapsto(\operatorname{coeff}_\alpha(p)m)_\alpha$ is bilinear and finitely supported, so the tensor universal property gives $F_M:P_n\otimes_A M\to M^{(E)}$. Define $G_M((m_\alpha))=\sum_\alpha X^\alpha\otimes m_\alpha$. It is linear. On a single supported coordinate $F_MG_M$ is the identity; on a pure tensor, $G_MF_M(p\otimes m)=\sum_\alpha X^\alpha\otimes a_\alpha m=p\otimes m$ by balancing. Pure tensors generate, so these are inverse isomorphisms. For $u:M\to N$, both routes send $p\otimes m$ to $(\operatorname{coeff}_\alpha(p)u(m))_\alpha$; this proves naturality.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product), universal property and bilinearity relations; explicit coefficient calculation supplying the monomial model in Tag 08QP.

proof.text: If $u:M\hookrightarrow N$ is injective, naturality identifies $P_n\otimes u$ with the map $(m_\alpha)\mapsto(u(m_\alpha))$, which is injective coordinatewise. The swap $m\otimes p\mapsto p\otimes m$ is a linear isomorphism with inverse the same swap, by the tensor universal property. Hence $u\otimes P_n$ is also injective, proving flatness by its definition. Now apply the cited flat-tensor exactness theorem with the commutative ring $A$ and the flat module $P_n$: tensoring on either side preserves every exact sequence.

source.place: Tag 00HD (lemma-flat), equivalence of injectivity preservation and exactness; explicit coordinatewise proof of injectivity.

proof.text: For every simplicial operator $h$ define $h'(p\otimes a')=h(p)\otimes a'$, and set $\epsilon'_n=\epsilon_n\otimes1$. Multiplication after scalar extension is $(p\otimes a')(r\otimes b')=pr\otimes a'b'$ with unit $1\otimes1$; it is induced by the bilinear extension of multiplication. Associativity, commutativity and the unit law follow on pure tensors from those of $P_n,A'$. Each $h'$ and $\epsilon'_n$ preserves these products and the unit. Scalar extension preserves composition and identities, so every simplicial and augmentation identity remains true. For $z=\sum_{j=1}^r b_j\otimes a'_j\in B'$, choose $p_j\in P_n$ with $\epsilon_n(p_j)=b_j$; then $\epsilon'_n(\sum_jp_j\otimes a'_j)=z$. Thus each new augmentation is surjective.

source.place: Tag 08QI (remark-resolution), polynomial and surjective augmentation data; Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), tensoring that data.

proof.text: Take $M=A'$ in Step 2. Its coefficient isomorphism identifies $P_n\otimes_A A'$ with $A'[X_i:i\in I_n]$ as an $A'$-module and sends $X^\alpha\otimes a'$ to $a'X^\alpha$. It is an algebra isomorphism: on two monomial tensors both the image of the product and the product of the images are $a'b'X^{\alpha+\beta}$, and $1\otimes1$ maps to $1$. Bilinearity and finite expansion give multiplicativity on all elements. This also proves the asserted normalization of the polynomial scalar-extension map.

source.place: Tag 08QP (lemma-flat-base-change), proof: the polynomial terms after scalar extension; monomial multiplication checks the specified map.

proof.text: In degree $-n$, both $TC$ and $s(P'_\bullet)$ have term $P_n\otimes_A A'$. For $n\ge1$, their differentials agree on $p\otimes a'$ because $(\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^id_i)(p)\otimes a'=\sum_{i=0}^n(-1)^i(d_i(p)\otimes a')$. At degree $0$ and in positive degrees their differentials are zero. Thus the identity components form a chain isomorphism $e:TC\to s(P'_\bullet)$ with inverse the same components. Both augmentations are zero away from degree $0$ and send $p\otimes a'$ to $\epsilon_0(p)\otimes a'$ at degree $0$, so $q'e=Tq$ with the specified target $T(B[0])=B'[0]$. The functor $Q_{A'}$ sends $e$ and its inverse to inverse arrows; set $\phi=Q_{A'}(e)$ and apply functoriality to obtain the required augmentation equality.
